docs.title: roman-cuts
docs.text: roman-cuts is a Python package designed to extract target-centered time-series image cutouts from observations taken with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Wide Field Instrument (WFI). It provides unified support for both simulated images (such as synthetic full-frame images generated with RImTimSim) and real Roman science data products accessed through the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST).

docs.title: About NASA Roman & the Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey
docs.text:
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is NASA's new flagship observatory, engineered to explore the infrared universe with unprecedented speed and precision. Its primary imaging camera, the Wide Field Instrument (WFI), combines 18 Sensor Chip Assemblies (SCAs) totaling 300 megapixels to yield a 0.281 deg² field of view—roughly 100 times that of the Hubble Space Telescope at comparable resolution (0.11 arcsec/pixel).

A cornerstone community initiative of Roman is the Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey (GBTDS). By continuously monitoring ~2 square degrees in the dense, dust-obscured Milky Way bulge with ~12-minute sampling over six 62-day seasons in the near-infrared, the GBTDS will detect tens of thousands of exoplanets via the transiting method, discover stellar oscillations, and measure billions of stellar positions.

docs.title: The TRExS Project: Transits in the Roman Galactic EXoplanet Survey
docs.text:
TRExS (Transits in the Roman Galactic EXoplanet Survey) is a Wide Field Science initiative and a Roman Cycle 1 designed to maximize the transit science return from Roman's GBTDS. While the GBTDS is nominally optimized for gravitational microlensing, its high-cadence time-series imaging of hundreds of millions of stars toward the Galactic Center makes it one of the most powerful transiting exoplanet surveys ever conceived.

Key pillars of TRExS include: - Massive Exoplanet Yields: TRExS is predicted to discover between ~100,000 transiting exoplanets, expanding the catalog of known exoplanets by orders of magnitude compared to Kepler and TESS. - Statistical Demographics of Rare Systems: The enormous sample size places stringent demographic constraints on intrinsically rare planetary architectures, ultra-short-period planets, planets orbiting evolved or giant stars, and brown dwarf companions. - Galactic Depth & Diversity: Probing deep through the Galactic disk into the inner bulge, TRExS observes stars across diverse stellar populations, metallicities, and Galactic environments, mapping how planet occurrence varies throughout the Milky Way. - Near-Infrared Atmospheres: Leveraging Roman's near-infrared bandpass (WFI F146 and companion filters), TRExS enables direct atmospheric detection and thermal emission measurements (e.g., secondary eclipses and phase curves) for thousands of transiting giant planets at a population level. - Survey Synergy: By pairing transit discoveries with microlensing detections in the same survey footprint, Roman and TRExS will establish a unified census of planetary systems spanning orbital separations from <0.1 AU out to free-floating planets.

Within the TRExS pipeline, roman-cuts serves as the primary data extraction layer, preparing target cutout cubes from full-frame images and cloud archives for downstream effective PSF (ePSF) modeling and precision light curve extraction.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: roman-cuts requires Python ≥ 3.11.

docs.title: User Installation with pip
docs.text:
Install the standard release (simulation module):

pip install roman-cuts

To install with Roman Commissioning (com) support—including cloud access, MAST archive queries, and Roman datamodels:

pip install "roman-cuts[com]"

Or install from a local repository clone:

git clone https://github.com/jorgemarpa/roman-cuts.git
cd roman-cuts
pip install -e ".[com]"

docs.title: Development Installation with uv
docs.text:
We recommend uv for fast, deterministic development environments:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/jorgemarpa/roman-cuts.git
cd roman-cuts

# Create virtual environment and install all dependencies (including dev and com extras)
uv sync --all-extras

# Run tests
uv run pytest -v

# Run linting and type checking
uv run ruff check .
uv run mypy src/

# Build and preview documentation locally
uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: roman-cuts provides two primary modules: 1. roman_cuts.sim: For simulated FITS images produced by RImTimSim or synthetic pipeline runs. 2. roman_cuts.com: For Roman Commissioning and archive observations queried from MAST or local ASDF/FITS L2 calibrated files.

docs.title: 1. Simulated Images (roman_cuts.sim)
docs.text:
The RomanCuts class processes simulated FITS images, accounting for telescope pointing shifts and dither patterns to extract time-series cutouts centered on sky coordinates.

from roman_cuts import RomanCuts

# Initialize from simulated FITS exposures
rc = RomanCuts.from_file("path/to/simulations/*.fits")

# Specify target sky coordinates (RA, Dec in degrees) and cutout size in pixels
ra = 268.5112137932491
dec = -29.24473947250156
cutout_size = 21  # 21x21 pixels

# Generate the cutout cube across all exposures
cutouts = rc.get_cutout(ra=ra, dec=dec, size=cutout_size)

# Export the cutout cube and metadata into an ASDF container
rc.to_asdf("target_cutout.asdf")

docs.title: 2. Roman Commissioning & Science Data (roman_cuts.com)
docs.text: The com module provides high-performance data access, archive queries via MAST, direct GWCS projections, and parallel cutout extraction for calibrated Roman L2 products.

docs.title: Querying MAST and Extracting Cutouts in Python
docs.text:
from roman_cuts.com import query_mast_files, make_cutout, run_cutout_pipeline

# Step 1: Query calibrated L2 files for a Roman observing program from MAST
files_df = query_mast_files(
    program="00234",          # Roman commissioning program ID
    file_type="cal",          # Calibrated exposure products
    sca=2,                    # Optional: filter by Sensor Chip Assembly (1-18)
)

# Step 2: Extract cutouts across the queried exposures in parallel
cutouts, metadata = make_cutout(
    file_list=files_df["uri"].tolist(),
    ra=268.5112,
    dec=-29.2447,
    size=25,
    parallel=True,
    max_workers=4,
)

# Step 3: Or execute the end-to-end pipeline and serialize directly to ASDF
run_cutout_pipeline(
    ra=268.5112,
    dec=-29.2447,
    size=25,
    program="00234",
    output="target_com_cutouts.asdf",
)

docs.title: Command-Line Interface
docs.text:
roman-cuts includes a dedicated CLI command for batch cutout extraction from Roman commissioning files:

# Query MAST and build an ASDF cutout file from the command line
roman-com-cutout --ra 268.5112 --dec -29.2447 --size 25 --program 00234 --output target_cutout.asdf

docs.title: roman_cuts.com — Commissioning & science data
docs.text:
Cutout utilities for Roman WFI commissioning and science data accessed via the MAST archive (cloud ASDF files, GWCS astrometry).

Install the extra dependencies before use:

pip install "roman-cuts[com]"

docs.title: query_mast_files
docs.text:
query_mast_files(
    program_id,
    detector,
    filter_name,
    file_type="l2",
    execution_plan=None,
    pass_num=None,
    segment=None,
    observation=None,
    visit=None,
    mission=None,
)

Query the MAST archive for Roman WFI files at a specific sky field.

Roman file names encode the full observation hierarchy as r{PPPPP}{CC}{AAA}{SSS}{OOO}{VVV}_{eeee}_{wfiss}_{filter}_{suffix}:

======= === ================================================================ Level Len Meaning ======= === ================================================================ Program 5 Observing program (program_id) ExecPlan 2 Execution plan within the program (execution_plan) Pass 3 Pass within the execution plan (pass_num); repeat visits of the same field across epochs share the same pass Segment 3 Segment within a pass (segment) Observ. 3 Observation within a segment (observation); this is the primary sky-field identifier — all exposures with the same observation number point to the same sky patch Visit 3 Visit (dither position) within an observation (visit) Exposure 4 Individual detector exposure ======= === ================================================================

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default program_id int

Roman program (proposal) ID, e.g. 1054.

required detector str or int

WFI detector. Any of 'WFI05', 'wfi05', 5, '05' are accepted and normalised to 'WFI##'.

required filter_name str

Optical element, e.g. 'F146' or 'f106'. Case-insensitive.

required file_type ``'l1'``, ``'l2'``, or ``'l4'``

Data level:

  • 'l1' – uncalibrated ramps (_uncal.asdf)
  • 'l2' – calibrated rate images (_cal.asdf) (default)
  • 'l4' – source catalogs (_cat.parquet)
'l2' execution_plan int

Execution plan number within the program (CC in the filename).

None pass_num int

Pass number within the execution plan (AAA). Different passes of the same observation cover the same sky at different epochs.

None segment int

Segment number within the pass (SSS).

None observation int

Observation number within the segment (OOO). This is the key parameter for selecting a specific field: all exposures sharing the same observation number are co-pointed.

None visit int

Visit (dither position) within the observation (VVV). Omit to retrieve all dithers at the field; supply to pin a single dither.

None mission `~astroquery.mast.MastMissions`

Authenticated mission object. When None, one is created from the MAST_API_TOKEN environment variable.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description products `~astropy.table.Table`

MAST product table. Each row is one file; products['filename'] can be passed directly to make_cutout.

docs.title: make_cutout
docs.text:
make_cutout(
    file_names,
    ra,
    dec,
    size=(10, 10),
    mission=None,
    verbose=False,
    lite=False,
    n_workers=8,
    backend="thread",
    strict=False,
)

Create pixel cutout cubes for one or more targets from Roman WFI L2 ASDF files.

The GWCS stored in each ASDF file maps (ra, dec) to detector pixel coordinates. Each cutout is extracted with ~astropy.nddata.Cutout2D (mode='partial'), which fills out-of-bounds pixels with NaN and handles coordinates near the detector edge gracefully. Targets that fall outside a file's footprint are kept as NaN entries.

Files are processed in parallel (one task per file; every target is cut from a file opened once) and the results are sorted by mid_time.

File access is dispatched by ~roman_cutouts.io._open_asdf, which auto-detects the execution platform (RRN, SMDC, standalone) via ~roman_cutouts.io._detect_platform. Supply mission to force the RRN/MAST path from any platform.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default file_names str or list of str

MAST product filenames (RRN), local/mounted-S3 paths (SMDC), plain local paths, or s3:// URIs.

required ra float or sequence of float

Right Ascension(s) of the cutout centre(s) in degrees (ICRS).

required dec float or sequence of float

Declination(s) of the cutout centre(s) in degrees (ICRS).

required size int, tuple of int, or list

Cutout size in pixels. An int gives a square cutout shared by all targets; a (ny, nx) tuple a shared rectangle; a list of ints or tuples gives one size per target (length one is broadcast).

(10, 10) mission `~astroquery.mast.MastMissions`

Authenticated mission object for RRN/MAST access. With backend="process" it is not shared; workers create their own from MAST_API_TOKEN.

None verbose bool

Print per-file pixel-coordinate messages when True.

False lite bool

Extract only the data plane (cube axis 0 has length 1).

False n_workers int

Number of parallel workers (capped at the number of files). 1 runs serially. Default 8.

8 backend ``'thread'`` | ``'process'``

'thread' (default) suits the I/O-bound workload and is safe in Jupyter and the CLI. 'process' uses a spawn process pool.

'thread' strict bool

Re-raise per-file errors instead of logging them and returning NaN.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description cutout_cubes list of ndarray

One per target, shape (n_types, n_files, ny, nx) where the first axis is [data, err, dq, dumo] (n_types=4, or 1 if lite).

metadatas list of `~pandas.DataFrame`

One per target, n_files rows with exposure, observation and instrument columns, mid_time, ra_target, dec_target and Cutout2D geometry fields. The boolean in_bounds column is False for NaN entries (target outside the file's footprint, or the file failed) and True otherwise, including partial overlaps, which are NaN-padded.

gwcsss list of list of `~astropy.wcs.wcsapi.HighLevelWCSWrapper`

One per target, n_files sliced GWCS objects (None for NaN entries). gwcsss[t][k].world_to_pixel(SkyCoord(...)) returns pixel coordinates in the cutout frame.

All outputs are sorted by ``mid_time``; entries with unknown time go last. A scalar *ra*/*dec* is one target, so each returned list has length 1.

docs.title: run_cutout_pipeline
docs.text:
run_cutout_pipeline(
    ra,
    dec,
    program_id,
    detector,
    filter_name,
    cutout_size,
    file_type="l2",
    execution_plan=None,
    pass_num=None,
    segment=None,
    observation=None,
    visit=None,
    max_files=None,
    output_path=None,
    mission=None,
    verbose=False,
    n_workers=8,
    backend="thread",
)

End-to-end pipeline: query MAST → extract cutouts → optionally save.

Combines query_mast_files, make_cutout, and save_to_asdf into a single callable that works from an interactive session, an import in another script, or the CLI via roman-make-cutout.

Observation hierarchy parameters (execution_plan … visit) are forwarded to query_mast_files; see that function's docstring for the full naming-convention table. Specifying observation is the minimum needed to pin a single field.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ra float or sequence of float

ICRS coordinates of the cutout centre(s) (degrees).

required dec float or sequence of float

ICRS coordinates of the cutout centre(s) (degrees).

required program_id int

Roman program ID.

required detector str or int

WFI detector ('WFI05', 5, '05' …).

required filter_name str

Optical element ('F146', 'f106' …).

required cutout_size int, tuple of int, or list

Cutout size in pixels (square, (ny, nx), or one per target).

required file_type ``'l1'`` | ``'l2'`` | ``'l4'``

Data level. Default 'l2'.

'l2' execution_plan int

Execution plan within the program.

None pass_num int

Pass (epoch) within the execution plan.

None segment int

Segment within the pass.

None observation int

Observation number — primary sky-field identifier.

None visit int

Visit (dither position) within the observation.

None max_files int

Cap on the number of files sent to make_cutout.

None output_path str

Directory in which to write the output ASDF file. None skips saving.

None mission `~astroquery.mast.MastMissions`

Authenticated mission object; auto-created from MAST_API_TOKEN when None.

None verbose bool

Forward verbose flag to make_cutout.

False n_workers int

Parallel workers used by make_cutout. Default 8.

8 backend ``'thread'`` | ``'process'``

Parallel backend used by make_cutout. Default 'thread'.

'thread'

Returns:

Name Type Description cutout_cubes list of ndarray or None

One cube per target, shape (4, n_files, ny, nx).

metadatas list of `~pandas.DataFrame` or None gwcsss list of list or None

All three are None when MAST returns no products.

docs.title: save_to_asdf
docs.text:
save_to_asdf(
    cutout_cube, metadata, gwcss, filename=None, n_workers=8
)

Serialise cutout cubes, metadata, and sliced GWCS lists to ASDF files.

One file is written per target. Pass the lists returned by make_cutout (N targets → N files) or the arrays of a single target. Multi-target saving writes concurrently using a thread pool.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cutout_cube ndarray or list of ndarray

Per-target cube(s), shape (n_types, n_files, ny, nx) ([data, err, dq, dumo], or data only when n_types == 1) or (n_files, ny, nx). A bare array is treated as one target.

required metadata `~pandas.DataFrame` or list of `~pandas.DataFrame`

Per-exposure metadata as returned by make_cutout.

required gwcss list or list of list

Per-cutout sliced GWCS objects (one list per target when cutout_cube is a list).

required filename str or list of str

Output file path(s) (*.asdf). With N > 1 targets it must be a list of length N. When None, each file is written to the current directory as cutouts_{pid}_{detector}_{filter}_{ra:.6f}_{dec:.6f}.asdf, with pid parsed from the leading PPPPP of the observation_id metadata column (PPPPPCCAAASSSOOOVVV), and detector (detector), filter (optical_element) and coordinates (ra_target, dec_target) also taken from the metadata. Missing values are written as unknown.

None n_workers int

Number of concurrent threads for writing ASDF files. Default 8.

8

Returns:

Type Description list of str

The paths written, one per target.

docs.title: roman_cuts.sim — Simulation data
docs.text: Cutout utilities for Roman WFI simulated images produced by the RImTimSim package. Data lives on local disk as individual FITS frames or pre-stacked ASDF cubes.

docs.title: RomanCuts
docs.text:
A class to create cutouts from Roman WFI simulated images created by TRExS group using the RImTimSim package.

The class provides access to: - Per frame WCS - Season average WCS - Cutout cubes (ntime, npix, npix) from the simulated FFI stack - Save cubes to disk as ASDF
